headline: Council votes down condo hotel zoning review, hears testimony on Bills 55 and 133

meeting.voteItem: County Communication 26-28 (proposed amendment to Bill 124, mutual aid with the County of Kauaʻi related to Hurricane Lowell)
meeting.summary: The Council voted down sending condo properties to the Maui Planning Commission for hotel zoning review. It heard testimony on Bill 55's six-year limit for ethics cases and Bill 133's safe parking pilot, and postponed County Communication 26-28 until Bill 124.
meeting.recap: It was the Council's last day in its chambers for a while, so the election crew can take over.[[0:04:57]] The Board of Ethics director supported Bill 55, which sets a six-year time limit to pursue ethics cases.[[0:13:07]] The prosecuting attorney asked for an investigator position to work full time on possible contractor fraud in Lahaina.[[0:16:46]] A testifier for a group serving houseless families said Bill 133 would let vehicles that are not fully registered join the safe parking pilot.[[0:28:20]] The Office of Hawaiian Affairs opposed Resolutions 26-160 and 26-161, which seek hotel zoning reviews for condo properties.[[0:38:21]] The Maui Vacation Rental Association supported both resolutions.[[0:55:00]] The recording ends at a ten-minute recess, with no vote yet on Bill 133.[[3:06:19]]
decided: The Council postponed this item until it takes up Bill 124.

moments.q: Moment of silence for Tasha Kama
Chair: "Not consistent, arbitrary, and often random."

issues.why: The chair said vacation rentals are being phased out of apartment districts, and new hotel districts were created for properties where continued rental use is appropriate.
